The diagram above shows a unit circle and the angle $\theta $ measured in the usual way. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $-0.64,$ calculate the reference angle ${\theta }_{R}$ to the nearest integer.

${\theta }_{R}≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
The reference angle is the acute angle that $\theta $ makes with the $x$-axis.

First, we create a right-triangle by drawing a vertical line from $P$ to the $x$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/6fdb497f69777c364f464e0ebd7ac4d4884679a3a38956da2818866d886614d2.png)

So, we have the following triangle, where ${\theta }_{R}$ is the reference angle of $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/9862a9d72f39e7f6d9abd861e4c3078cb67962d50548fae8ee98a634f262fed6.png)

We know that the hypotenuse has a length of $1$ because it is a radius of the unit circle. 

Now, using the triangle above, we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{\theta }_{R}=\frac{0.64}{1}=0.64.
$$

Now, we compute the angle ${\theta }_{R}$ using the inverse sine:

$$
{\theta }_{R}=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.64)≈{40}^{∘}
$$
